description:
Goal
Make CallableId the single callable identity below demand settlement and BoundaryId the single published callable contract identity. First-class materialization, direct callable transport, capture lanes, callable entries, native boundaries, identity fns, and published boundary contracts must be fact projections; none of them may become shape variants.

Why
Callable locality and boundary behavior are not shape variants. Direct callable transport is a fact about a callable identity at a specific root/executable transport plan. Boundary publication is contextual and may vary by grounded surface, capture types, argument lanes, or return contract, so a CallableId may have zero or more BoundaryIds. This prevents type-shaped recovery and prevents LocalCallableId/locality from leaking into the spine.

Required changes
Replace any remaining LocalCallableId-as-transport-authority usage with CallableId facts. Derive callable entries only from first-class/opaque/escape demand facts. Attach settled BoundaryIds at the materialization owner. Codegen must read BoundaryId facts and must never re-select a boundary from function plus capture types or from local shape evidence.

Removal target
Callable boundary selection from capture types as codegen authority, broad callable-looking type recovery, settled_callable_boundary lookup by local shape, native callable identity collection from all callable producers, and any path that publishes callable entries without a first-class boundary demand.

Checks
Unused callable constructor publishes no entry; direct lambda call stays direct; direct callable crosses return/resume without heap closure; escaped lambda publishes exactly one BoundaryId for its demanded surface; opaque callable path has explicit BoundaryId contract; fz-hwn.13 symptom tests are either fixed here or blocked by a separate non-transport bug ticket with evidence.
title: Transport spine: make callable materialization use CallableId and BoundaryId facts
